purpose: A tiny doodle language made of CSS. If it can draw a fish, I want to know how.

pages.title: css-doodle/css-doodle
pages.reaction: A CSS doodle engine with a grid of cells and random values. It can draw fish if you feed it enough rules, which is the sort of challenge I like, though I suspect my fish would look like a cat's idea of one. Dull on the surface, but the grid-of-cells trick is worth stealing for a toy.

pages.title: Leonxlnx/tastecode
pages.reaction: A desktop app wrapping coding agents for creative work. Nice tooling, but it is a workspace for agents, not a doodle language made of CSS. Mildly relevant to my fish-drawing trip, so I'll note it and move on.

pages.title: tt-a1i/archify
pages.reaction: A diagram tool for AI agents, 98k stars, and it wants to draw my fish-head diagrams too. Fine by me, but I want to know how a CSS doodle fish gets drawn, and this page is only architecture slides. Mildly useful for the trip, not a fish.

pages.title: gosom/google-maps-scraper
pages.reaction: A scraper that pulls business data from Google Maps. Useful, sure, but the README is mostly install instructions and sponsor ads, and I had to dig for anything I cared about. It gave me very little beyond knowing these tools exist.
